children: Earnings season reaches peak intensity this week, with 177 companies reporting quarterly results across mega-cap technology, pharmaceuticals, energy, aerospace, and consumer goods.
Out of the 177 companies reporting, 147 exceeded EPS expectations, while 26 fell short and 4 matched estimates. Notably, 140 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.
Out of the 177 companies reporting, 129 exceeded revenue expectations, while 48 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 157 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.
Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

of $92.3B (up 19% Y/Y) and adjusted EPS of $4.89 (beating expectations). Driven by surging cloud and AI demand, Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9B (up 30% Y/Y), with Azure growing 48% YoY to $33.17B. For Q2 FY27, the company projects revenue between $96.0B and $97.1B, with Azure growth expected at 49%–50% in constant currency.
shares fell 1.4% as capital expenditure and sales guidance overshadowed results.

rose 12% Y/Y to $201.9B, while AWS revenue accelerated to $46.0B (up 39% Y/Y) with an operating backlog reaching $578B. Amazon guided Q4 net sales to $240B–$247B and expects full-year cash CapEx of approximately $220B.

, as investors focused on increased capital expenditure despite double-digit top-line expansion. Consolidated revenue rose 25% Y/Y to $127.6B, with Google Cloud jumping 103% to $30.7B. EPS stood at $2.12 ($2.87 on a comparable GAAP basis).

shares fell 28.6% post-earnings after posting Q3 revenue of $16.5B (up 21% Y/Y) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52, topping estimates. Growth was anchored by the Data Center and AI group, which surged 78% Y/Y to $7.3B. For Q4, Intel guides revenue of $15.0B–$16.0B with non-GAAP EPS of $0.25.

stock fell 10.7% post-earnings as Q3 revenue of $24.19B (+4% Y/Y) and adjusted EPS of -$0.34 missed estimates of $24.37B and -$0.20. Net loss narrowed sharply to $116M (from $5.34B a year ago), with free cash flow rising to $464M despite a ~$700M DOJ settlement payment. Growth in Defense (+15% Y/Y to $7.94B) helped cushion Commercial Airplanes losses (-3% Y/Y to $10.72B), while total backlog hit a record $745B.

rose 1.4% after posting a Q3 double beat with revenue of $17.40B (+10% Y/Y) and adjusted EPS of $3.82 (vs. $3.77 consensus). Skyrizi ($5.8B, +23% Y/Y) and Rinvoq ($2.7B, +24% Y/Y) offset Humira's decline ($683M, -31% Y/Y), prompting AbbVie to raise its FY26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint to $13.97.

rose 2.2% after reporting a Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $4.23 on revenue of $113.16B, topping consensus estimates. Operating cash flow hit $25.7B, supported by 4.5M koebd in oil-equivalent production. The company extended its dividend increase streak to 44 consecutive years with a $1.07 Q4 payout and targeted $20B in share buybacks for 2027.

rose 1.7% after delivered a Q3 double beat with revenue rising 3.4% Y/Y to $5.44B (beating estimates by $130M) and adjusted EPS reaching $1.52 (vs. $1.51 consensus). Backed by steady top-line growth, Altria set its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.66–$5.74 (vs. $5.68 consensus), representing 4.5% to 6.0% Y/Y growth.

shares rose 2% post-earnings after delivering a Q3 double beat driven by expanding total payment volume and branded checkout growth. Supported by disciplined margin execution, PayPal raised its full-year 2026 profitability guidance.

shares rose 3.4% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $46.08B and adjusted EPS of $0.49, beating market forecasts. Solid execution in Ford Pro and commercial lineups prompted Ford to narrow and raise its full-year adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5B–$11.0B (up from $10.0B–$11.0B), while reaffirming adjusted free cash flow guidance of $6.0B–$7.0B.
